extracted.intended_audience: memoir writers and writers of first-person literary fiction; creative writing students and teachers
extracted.subtask_description: Craft principles and evaluative tests for writing (and critiquing) memoir or first-person literary fiction, emphasizing voice, memory, sensory detail, and ethical honesty. Guidance covers what to select, how to shape material, and how to test quality of scenes and narrative stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice Is Everything
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each great memoir lives or dies based 100 percent on voice." Establishing authentic literary voice requires confronting both your good and bad qualities. "Whatever people like about you will manifest on the page, and what drives them crazy will keep you humble; you'll need both sides of yourself to hold a reader's attention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice must feel inhabited rather than performed; it should carry personality's appealing and irritating aspects. Use the narrator's specific tonal choices and self-revelations to sustain reader interest across the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Truth Contract
rubrics_metrics.description: With the reader. Memoir relies on memory, which is fallible. The memoirist must strive for truth within those limits. (For first-person fiction: parallel implicit contract about authenticity of internal experience.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge memory's limits rather than pretending omniscience; maintain an implicit honesty about what is remembered versus reconstructed. Readers expect truthful effort even if every detail cannot be proven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnality / Sensory Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The text's "carnality" — its sensual data, leveraged to create multidimensional reader experience. Karr argues sensory detail is the path into emotional truth, not adjacent to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete sensory specifics (taste, smell, texture, sound, visual detail) as primary means to access and convey emotional truth. Treat sensory detail as the vehicle for feeling rather than mere ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Inner Enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Each memoirist (each first-person narrator) has an inner antagonist — a self-deception, blind spot, or moral failing. The book becomes interesting when the writer faces it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and dramatize the narrator's self-deceptions or moral flaws; the narrative tension often comes from the author's struggle against their own tendencies. Avoid flattening the narrator into a one-note victim or hero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory's Texture
rubrics_metrics.description: Show how memory works — its gaps, its sensory hooks, its contradictions. Don't pretend to remember everything; lean into the partial, hauntological quality of recall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly depict the uneven, associative nature of recollection (what returns vividly and what is lost). Use this texture as part of narrative strategy—gaps, contradictions, and sensory triggers can be dramatized rather than smoothed over.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting Memory
rubrics_metrics.description: The memoirist (and novelist working from life) curates radically. The 5 minutes that make the chapter are chosen from 10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ruthlessly selective: choose the few moments that carry emotional or narrative weight and excise the rest. Craft scenes so that each chosen moment justifies its space and contributes to thematic/structural shaping.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Risk of Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Karr argues the great memoirs require risking the writer's own image — admitting what's shameful, ridiculous, or pathetic. Same for fiction with significant interiority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willingness to risk reputation and expose personal flaws strengthens credibility and moral complexity. Avoid defensive self-justification; let vulnerability serve aesthetic and ethical aims rather than score-settling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice feels inhabited, not performed
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the voice feel inhabited, not performed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrator's tone and perspective arise organically from character and circumstance rather than from artifice or affectation. Performance undermines trust and reader immersion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenes are specific (place, time, sense)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scenes for concrete anchors—clear setting, temporal markers, and sensory information. Specificity helps scenes feel lived-in and supports verisimilitude; it also supplies the carnality that yields emotional truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator confronts uncomfortable truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the narrator confront uncomfortable truth?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether the narrator acknowledges difficult facts about themselves, relationships, or events. Confrontation of uncomfortable truth is central to moral movement in memoir and keeps the narrative ethically engaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid score-settling and self-mythologizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the work avoid score-settling and self-mythologizing?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for retaliatory or vindictive passages aimed at settling scores; such tendencies corrupt the truth contract and reduce credibility. Likewise, avoid inflating the self into mythic proportions—humility and nuance produce stronger work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure shaped, not just chronological
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the structure shaped, not just chronological?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the narrative order is deliberately organized for thematic or emotional progression rather than merely following time. A 'shaped' structure uses selection, juxtaposition, and pacing to create meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small details are load-bearing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether specific small details carry weight—recurring motifs, telling sensory notes, or minute behaviors that advance character, theme, or emotional impact. Eliminate details that are merely decorative.
